- text: THE ULTIMATE SPIDER PLANT CARE GUIDE
- img "🪴"
- img "☀️"
- text: LIGHT
- generic: Place them in bright light near an (unshaded) east, south or west window. Keep them out of direct sun outdoors to avoid scorched leaves.
- img "💧"
- text: WATER AND TAP WATER WARNING
- generic: Water only when completely dry. Spider plants are extremely sensitive to fluoride, chlorine, and salts in tap water, which cause brown leaf tips. Use distilled water, rainwater, or reverse osmosis to keep the foliage happy.
- img "👶"
- text: BABIES AND BLOOMS
- generic: To trigger spiderettes, keep the plant slightly root-bound in bright light. Once the offset plantlets form tiny roots at their bases, snip them off and put them directly into damp soil or water to root.
- img "🪴"
- text: SOIL AND POTTING
- generic: Plant in a light, fast-draining mix of 2 parts standard potting soil and 1 part perlite. Spider plants have thick, fleshy tubered roots that store water, so use a pot with drainage holes to prevent root rot.
- img "🌡️"
- text: TEMP AND HUMIDITY
- generic: They thrive in standard home temperatures between 60°F and 80°F. Average indoor humidity works fine, but higher humidity prevents the leaf tips from drying out.
- img "🧪"
- text: FEEDING
- generic: Feed LIGHTLY once a month during spring and summer with an organic balanced houseplant fertilizer diluted to half strength. Avoid over-fertilizing, as excess salts will burn the root tips and cause brown leaf margins.
